ttft.title: TTFT Performance
ttft.description: Configure RPM/TPM, input tiers, and rounds. Supports streaming vs non-streaming requests with live per-request logs and P50/P90 summary.
ttft.requestModeHint: Stream: first SSE token (standard TTFT). Non-stream: full JSON response time (≈ total latency, no first token).
ttft.slaNoteNonStream: Non-stream mode: TTFT equals full response time; not comparable to streaming TTFT. Use SLA for same-mode comparison only.
ttft.rpmHint: Requests per minute — determines how many requests per tier per round
ttft.durationMinHint: How long to send at RPM for each tier in each round
ttft.roundsHint: Repeat the full test this many times (sweep all selected tiers each round)
ttft.selectTiersHint: Select one or more input length tiers
ttft.slaNote: Criterion: TTFT P90 (valid when success rate ≥ 99%)
ttft.noData: Configure settings and click Start test
ttft.noTiersSelected: Select at least one input tier
ttft.successRateLow: Success rate below 99% — metrics are indicative only

otps.title: OTPS Throughput
otps.description: Measure output tokens per second across concurrency steps. OTPS is valid only when success rate ≥ 99%.
otps.maxTokensHint: Large enough for a stable generation segment (512–2048 recommended)
otps.requestsPerLevelHint: Requests sent at each concurrency level
otps.slaNote: Criterion: OTPS P50 at highest concurrency with success rate ≥ 99%; >10B compares L1≥30 and L2≥10
otps.noData: Configure API and settings, then start OTPS test

accuracy.title: Accuracy Acceptance
accuracy.description: Compare benchmark scores against official disclosed results. Some datasets are bundled locally for API-based evaluation in the browser.
accuracy.limitationsBody: This module is for API acceptance (stable reasoning + answers), not a definitive capability leaderboard.
accuracy.limitationsAime: AIME2026 has only 30 items and is widely public (HuggingFace, etc.). Frontier models (e.g. DeepSeek V4) may have seen them in training — high scores do not rule out memorization; small runs are noisy (1 miss in 5 = −20%).
accuracy.limitationsGpqa: GPQA-Diamond (198 items) discriminates better, but top models are near saturation (90%+) and the set is also public.
accuracy.limitationsHarness: We use single-shot temperature=0 and simple integer/letter grading. Official leaderboards often use multi-sample runs and symbolic graders (math_verify). Scores are not directly comparable — use ±2pt acceptance only.
accuracy.localRunBody: Question files live under public/benchmarks/ (served at /benchmarks/ in dev). Whether you can score them depends on the dataset:
accuracy.localRunAime: AIME2026 (30): Yes — load local file → call your API → grade answers in-browser.
accuracy.localRunSwe: SWE-Bench Pro (731 prompts): No auto score — preview only; full eval needs Docker + unit tests.
accuracy.manualHint: Not bundled locally. Requires HF access or dedicated harness — enter results manually after external run.
accuracy.toleranceNoteBody: Doc: measured vs official within ±2–4 percentage points passes. Default tolerance: ±2 points.

leaderboard.title: Accuracy score charts
leaderboard.subtitle: Only the two benchmarks you can run here: AIME2026 and GPQA-Diamond. Green bars are measured on this site after a run.
leaderboard.disclaimer: Public references from BenchLM.ai (Jul 2026) and similar leaderboards; harnesses may differ. GLM-5.1 official/doc rows are from the acceptance document. Do not compare directly with local runs.

aime2026.why: Required by acceptance doc; meant as fresh-year problems, but now widely public — interpret high frontier scores with contamination risk in mind.

gpqaDiamond.desc: Graduate-level science multiple choice — 198 Diamond questions.

sweBenchPro.desc: Real GitHub issues — model must produce a patch; graded by unit tests.
sweBenchPro.why: Long-horizon coding; official ~58.4%. Local bundle is prompts only — no in-browser grading.

hle.desc: Humanity's Last Exam — 2500 expert questions, multimodal.
hle.why: Official ~52.3%. Requires HF agreement; ~274MB — not bundled.

tauBench.why: Official ~70.6%. Needs tau2-bench simulator, not a flat question file.
